approval.rationale: Campaign 5 Option D (Regime/Error Analysis) configuration frozen and authorized per B4 owner decision packet signed by PMED on 2026-10-22. Approval mode stays autonomous_revalidation: every proposal is revalidated against current ledger state at approval time; no hidden human selection. champion_integrity_policy.champion_regression_handling: Promotion remains allowed under the predeclared parent rule (no gate weakening); a true regression vs the standing champion must be recorded as champion_regression=true in the ledger row and in the version snapshot, so the champion line is auditable. Never silently overwrite a better absolute scorer without the flag.
champion_integrity_policy.note: Carried forward from Campaign 4 to maintain champion line integrity.

holdout_policy.rule: prospective/ never opened, never cited, never generated

multiplicity_policy._note: Carried forward from Campaign 4. Family-wise alpha 0.05, week_level_signflip_holm method with M=1000. Flip draw from C4 remains frozen (seed + rows hash pinned).
multiplicity_policy.feasibility_rule: n_boot + 1 >= 20 * m AND n_flips + 1 >= 20 * m for every declared family; otherwise freeze blocked (fail-closed)

flip_draw.flip_W_source: documented frozen OOF evaluation frame: 41,221 rows / 157 ISO weeks / pi=0.165 (D2 review, D2_REVIEW_SUPERSESSION_NOTE_2026_10_13.md, H10_SIGNFLIP_PORT_SPEC_2026_10_13.md section 9); the recorded rows hash binds the actual frame W at use time
flip_draw.procedure: Case A: drawn once at configuration freeze by secrets.randbits(64) (OS CSPRNG, data-independent) before any Campaign 4 outcome exists; recorded here and never redrawn. Production callers obtain it via signflip.load_campaign_flip_draw and fail closed (FlipProvenanceMissing) on any stage/W/hash mismatch. Campaign 5 reuses the C4 flip draw.

multiplicity_policy.mc_resolution_note: At M=1000 the minimum representable p is 1/1001; at Holm's first threshold a member must produce the minimum representable p to survive for m in 36-50, and borderline members are resolved with 25-48% probability, always biased toward non-rejection. Disclosed in the campaign-end record note.
multiplicity_policy.missing_member_effect: Counting an unavailable member toward m at p=1.0 STRICTENS, never loosens, the remaining members' Holm thresholds (corrected wording; the pinned decision sheet's 'thresholds are unchanged' is wrong -- see D2_REVIEW_SUPERSESSION_NOTE_2026_10_13.md item 1).
multiplicity_policy.n_flips_note: M = the week-level sign-flip count. The recorded feasibility must include M: the p-value's resolution is 1/(M+1), so a formal refutation at Holm's first threshold alpha/m is attainable only while M + 1 >= 20*m. feasibility() now enforces both counts and treats a missing M as infeasible (never silently feasible).
multiplicity_policy.p_value_note: Adopted method (b): week-level sign-flip Monte-Carlo p-values at M=1000 with Holm step-down (familywise alpha=0.05), computed by the production port with recorded, data-independent flip-draw provenance (see multiplicity_policy.flip_draw). Validity is procedure-level (Result 2'-B, marginal over the recorded flip draw), never conditional on the realized flip set; Result 2 is retracted. The campaign-end record discloses the Monte-Carlo resolution limitation (min representable p = 1/1001; borderline members at large m resolved 25-48%, biased toward non-rejection) and the C-2 Option A missing-member rule (strictens, never loosens).
